record.original_question: Is there a function f(g) such that every 5-connected graph embedded in a genus-g surface with face-width at least f(g) contains a Hamiltonian cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.2 There is a function f (g) such that every 5-connected graph embedded on a surface of genus g with face-width at least f (g) contains a Hamiltonian cycle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_g$ denote a closed surface of Euler genus $g$. For a graph $G$ 2-cell embedded in $\Sigma_g$, the face-width (representativity) of the embedding is the minimum, over all non-contractible simple closed curves $C$ in $\Sigma_g$, of $|C \cap G|$ (the number of points where $C$ meets $G$, with $C$ chosen to meet $G$ only in vertices).

Question: Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ such that for every nonnegative integer $g$, every 5-connected graph $G$ that admits a 2-cell embedding in a surface of Euler genus $g$ with face-width at least $f(g)$ contains a Hamiltonian cycle?
artifact.status_search_result: The general conjecture remains open. It has been verified for triangulations by Yu, and Thomas–Yu showed that 5-connected toroidal graphs are Hamiltonian. Recent work establishes exponentially many Hamiltonian cycles in 5-connected triangulations of large face-width on fixed surfaces, but the conjecture for general (non-triangulation) 5-connected embedded graphs with large face-width is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Cycles in 5-connected triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: It has been conjectured that any 5-connected graph embedded in a surface with sufficiently large face-width is hamiltonian. This was verified by Yu for the triangulation case but is still open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is open in general; the triangulation case is settled.

status_evidence.title: Five-Connected Toroidal Graphs Are Hamiltonian
status_evidence.snippet: Every edge in a 5-connected graph embedded in the torus is contained in a Hamilton cycle.
